title: Ser + Participle: Who Built and Who Was Expelled

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the passive with *ser* + past participle from B1 Unit 18: *La ley fue aprobada por el Parlamento*. The participle agrees with the subject, and *por* names who did the action. It fits a story about the past, where you want to put the thing that was done first: the churches, the scores, the missionaries.

sections.title: Passive sentences about the missions
rows: Las misiones fueron fundadas por jesuitas.
The missions were founded by Jesuits. (feminine plural: *fundadas*)
The Jesuits were expelled in 1767. (masculine plural: *expulsados*)
La iglesia fue restaurada en el siglo XX.
The church was restored in the twentieth century. (feminine singular: *restaurada*)
Seis misiones fueron declaradas Patrimonio de la Humanidad en 1990.
Six missions were declared World Heritage Sites in 1990.

items.spanish: Los templos fueron construidos con madera de la región.
items.english: The churches were built with wood from the region.

items.spanish: Las partituras fueron encontradas en los archivos de las misiones.
items.english: The scores were found in the archives of the missions.

items.spanish: La música barroca es tocada hoy por orquestas locales.
items.english: Baroque music is played today by local orchestras.

sections.content: Check the ending of the participle: it matches the subject, not the doer. *Los templos fueron construidos por los indígenas y los misioneros*: *construidos* agrees with *los templos*. Use *por* only when you want to name the doer.
